reply.text:
Grip failing before your back does is common, and it's fixable. Here's what I'd do:

1. Hang from the bar for time at the end of a session, a few sets of as long as you can hold. Build up the total over the weeks.
2. Grip the bar hard, as if you're trying to bend it, and keep your thumb wrapped around it. A tight grip also helps the lats fire.
3. Avoid chalk-free sweaty hands: chalk or a dry towel makes a real difference.
4. Heavy carries (farmer's walks, heavy dumbbells at your sides) a couple of times a week train grip without adding much fatigue.
5. Don't chase grip work on the same day you're trying to max out pull-up reps. Do the pull-ups first, then the grip work after.

Straps are fine on high-volume back days when the goal is your lats, but I'd keep most of your pull-up work strap-free so the grip catches up.

If you want, I can add farmer's carries or dead hangs to your program.
